decontamination_notes: cii-v2 candidate #4 under the hard-band gate (best model <=2/3). EPIC composing two undici PRs that touch the same file a day apart: #5515 'store revalidation-only responses so etag revalidation can engage' (merged 2026-07-16; SUPERSEDES community attempt #4624, whose first pass was judged structurally wrong) and #5514 'invalidate Location and Content-Location URIs on unsafe methods' (merged 2026-07-17, fixes #5509). Both are RFC 9111 conformance work — convention-heavy semantics (revalidation-only storage, SHOULD-level invalidation of named URIs, relative-reference resolution, same-origin restriction) that interact with the interceptor's storage, freshness, and invalidation paths. Base is the parent of #5515's merge; verified only these two PRs touched lib/handler/cache-handler.js in the window (4 total commits); gold is the two-PR diff of that single file. Repo sliced without upstream test/ to keep the slice lean; tests run against the package root via require('./index.js'). HARNESS SUBTLETY documented for maintainers: at this base, interceptors composed onto a bare Client are silently inert when dispatch options carry no origin (the later-fixed interceptors-origin regression, itself a v1 task) — all hidden tests therefore pass origin explicitly in each request, which was verified to make the cache engage at base (fresh responses served from cache, hits=1). Built by differential probing in-image: 9 scenarios; 5 diverge base-vs-gold (ETag+no-cache and ETag+max-age=0 revalidation with If-None-Match and 304-from-store, POST Location invalidation, Content-Location invalidation targeting a DIFFERENT URI than the request, relative Location resolution) and form the 5 fail_to_pass tests; 4 verified-stable scenarios are the guards (fresh-from-cache, request-URI self-invalidation, no-store, cross-origin Location must NOT invalidate — the same-origin check matters in both directions). Loopback servers only (work under the network-off sandbox). Assertions use origin hit counts, response bodies, and observed request headers; never library message text. Per the v2 charter: no fix-location hints; issue states the two behaviors and the RFC constraints, not the implementation.
